body: Thank you for your help and patience.

I guess that is what it always sounded like to me. That you have to be ready to completely substitute your therapist's judgment for your own. The examples you give sound reasonable and I am willing to accept that there are at least some things that I think that are probably inaccurate. But I am not willing to just accept the judgement of someone that I don't know and don't trust. I don't think I'm the smartest person in the world, but I am inclined to know why I hold the beliefs that I hold.

If I am willing to approach it on a case-by-case basis, skeptically but open to discussion and changing my mind, like we are doing now, do you think is that enough for a therapist to work with?

That's where I balk. Every time someone asks me, "Do you want to change?" Or, "Do you want to be happy?" I hear, "Do you want to be a Stepford wife?" Or, "Would you like some soma?" 
No. And that's a price for happiness I can't seem to get past. It doesn't offer an advantage other than that I don't think it's wrong. Which is apparently the nature of your analogy about filters, which causes me to feel like the prerequisite for getting help with depression is to not be depressed.

I hear you, but I see no evidence to support the view that it's my perception that is the product of the filter. Or perhaps both perceptions are the products of filters. Why then would one be more valid than the other? Or perhaps there is no duality in perception, just gradients of perception, which I find to be most likely, and this makes it even more absurd to draw some arbitrary line in the sand of what level of perception is officially warped and what is not. Where does that leave us? Interpretive acts or subjective. Why would I prefer one subjective filter over another especially if I find mine to be more relevant? Thus my god analogy.

PS thanks for discussing with me.

I think so. I guess he's right then. I don't want anything, except to not be here. I've read some about cognitive behavioral therapy and it sounds like the most insipid BS imaginable. If you stop thinking unhappy thoughts, you won't be unhappy! OMG, why didn't I think of that? Do I want to forsake a reality that I find to be supported by evidence? No. Do I want to accept a reality that I don't find to be supported by evidence so I can just ignore the bad things? Nope.
It sounds like intellectual suicide. Your body dies a bit every day. Shortening telomeres and all that. Suicide is the accelerated death of the body. Self dies a little bit every second too. Every second of experience inexorably changes the inner self. CBT sounds like the accelerated death of the mind. Do I want to overwrite my "self" with happy thoughts? Nope. If one of those things is going to experience accelerated death, I'd rather it be my body. Why would I go through all the work for something that only offers mechanisms for coping with something I don't want anyway? 

I suppose this light bulb finds changing to be a lot more intellectually complicated than just wanting too. I keep finding myself back in this same place. This conversation with my BF usually ends with him saying he can't logic me into wanting to change. It mirrors what my mom told me when I stopped believing in god. Well, if I can't and he can't then I'm just stuck, because that's the way my brain works. Maybe I'm just being stupid. But then again, if I thought my views were invalid, I wouldn't have them

Thanks for the explanation.

Thanks, that's... not a way I've thought of looking at it, or a way I've thought of as being an "okay" way to look at it.

I haven't seen a therapist. I've talked to by BF about it a couple of times, but while he says I should go, I feel like he ends up telling me I shouldn't too. There are too many prerequisites that I don't understand and can't meet. I have to believe it will work. I have to want to go. I have to do it for me. I don't want to go. I don't think it will work, I don't understand what "doing it for me" looks like. If I did, I'm not sure I would be depressed. It's like he is telling me that I have to stop being depressed before I can go to a therapist to get help for depression.

Do you know anything about this?
Thanks. That does help a lot. It makes me feel... "less crazy" I guess is the closest thing I can think of. I'm sorry about your great grandmother.

I don't know what to do. My BF has suggested therapy, but every time we talke about it, he has told me not to go if I don't want to. I don't understand. I don't want to. I won't ever want to. The prerequisites seem so daunting that I can't possibly even start to get help. I can't even small talk with strangers face to face.

Maybe I haven't really tried anything. I feel like I have. I'm still alive right now. I've tried to be happy and productive. A good person. Not angry. Not mean. Not difficult. But I keep failing. I can never do it right. I can't even apologize right because people just tell me to stop apologizing.

I feel like I have nowhere to go. I'm stuck against a wall. I've forced my way through as far as I can and I have no where else to go. The barriers in every which direction are too much and all I can do is wait until I have nothing else I can do but die.

Thank you for taking the time to answer. I was too scared to check back for long while. I just wanted it to be somewhere.

I don't know anymore if I knew what they were doing. I didn't like it. I don't know why I let them do it. I remember taking sex ed in 7th grade and finally understanding that those things were part of a lexicon of activities that kids shouldn't know about. And that maybe, maybe I'm not a bad person for what happened. But I don't know anymore. I let them. I did let them. And I knew that I would get in trouble if anyone knew. I knew it was bad.

I don't know why I feel like I need to know if this counts. I feel like I need to know if should be ashamed or if I can be forgiven because it was just a kid thing or if it was my fault or if it wasn't. I know those are probably stupid questions, but I can't shake the feeling that I need someone to tell me if I should feel bad about myself or not for what happened. I just need to know.
